key_insight: Cluster LOCO measures how much each feature matters for clustering by checking how much cluster generalizability drops when that feature is removed.
engineering_relevance: This gives practitioners a model-agnostic way to audit, interpret, and prioritize features in clustering workflows, including large-scale scientific datasets.
method: Split data, cluster one part, and test how well the learned labels generalize to held-out samples.
Compute feature importance by leaving one covariate out and measuring the drop in clustering generalizability.
Scale the approach with Cluster LOCO-MP, a minipatch ensemble variant for large datasets.
evidence_signal: The authors evaluate on synthetic simulations and single-cell transcriptomics, reporting that Cluster LOCO more reliably identifies informative features than existing clustering feature-importance methods.
watch_item: Because the score depends on clustering stability and data splitting choices, results may vary with the clustering algorithm, split design, and dataset size.
paper_title: Cluster LOCO: Feature Importance For Interpreting Clusters
